main_text.l: מִסְנָּרֶת Taenia, quasi Circumclusionem dicas, Exod.25. v.25. Aff. לְמִסְנָּרָתוֹ Ad taniam ejus, ibid.
מִסְגְּרוֹת f.p. Clausurae, Fasciae, quasi Circumclusiones dicta, 1.Reg.7.28. Cum Aff. מִסְגְּרוֹתָם De conclavibus, claustris suis, 2.Sam.22.46.
סַךְ m. Cippus, Compes: בְּסַּד In compede, Job.13. v.27. & 33.11. Quaedam exemplaria habent סַד quasi סוד.
סָדִין m. Sindon, Prov.31. v.24. Plural. סְדִינִים Sindones, Jud.14.12.

סָדַר m. Ordo: סְדָרִים Ordines, Job.10.22. & ם in ש mutato, שִׁדְרוֹת f. Ordinationes, Coaxationes, 1.Reg.6.9. הַשְּׁדְרוֹת Ordines hos, sc. armatorum, 1.Reg.11. v.8.15. Verbum סָדַר Ordinare, Disponere, Chaldaeis & Rabbinis tritissimum est.
מִסְדְּרוֹנָת[?] f. προαύλιον[?] Procaeton, Vestibulum in quo custodes principum excubant, Jud.2.23.
סָהַר m. Rotunditas: אֲגַן הַסַּהַר Crater rotunditatis, Cant.7.2. id est, rotundus.
סוֹהַר m. Turris, Carcer, à rotunditate aedificii, Genes.39. vers.20.
שַׁחֲרוֹנִים[?] m. Lunulae, ornamenta sive monilia pretiosa, à lunari forma sic appellata, Jud.8.16.21. Jes.3.18. à Chaldaeo סַהְרָא Luna, quòd plena, Rotunda est.

סוּג Avertit se, Retrocessit: Praeterit. סָג Retrocessit, Psal.53.4. Particip. Praeter. סוּג לֵב Aversus animo, Prov.14.14. Et ex Chaldaica significatione, Foemina, סוּגָה Sepitus, Cant.7.2. (Rabbinis סֵךְ Sepes,) Futur. in Cholem, יָסוּג Retrocedemus, Psal.80.9. Niph. נָסוּג Retroactus vel Aversus fuit, Avertit se: נָסוּג לֹא אחור לבנו Non agitur retrorsum animus noster, Ps.44.19. Et cum ש loco Samech, נָשׂוּג Retrocedebat, Aversum

page.notes: Running head and headwords are Hebrew; the Greek word after the f. in the Procaeton entry and the Hebrew headwords סַךְ, סוֹהַר, שַׁחֲרוֹנִים, מִסְדְּרוֹנָת and סוּג are doubtful in their vowels and letters, and are marked [?] where uncertain. The number "33.11." after Job is partly blurred. The long s is printed as f throughout and is transcribed as plain s (Genes., vers., Jes., Psal., Ps., noster, se, Retrocessit). The text ends mid-entry at "Aversum", which continues on the next page. The signature "Ii" is followed by a bare "4", transcribed as "Ii 4".
